items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: He said I want you to play with me, he said because you've got that old style of playing that I like.

ctx.x: So that night he told me, he said, George, how would you like to work regularly with me? He said I'll get in the playing of work. I said well, I said George I'll tell you. I've been off these things so long and I'm trying to get back into them. He said well I think you're doing nicely. He said I want you to play with me, he said because you've got that old style of playing that I like. He said because I'm not going to change the none of this modern stuff they're playing. He said I'm holding on to the authentic.…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: My name is Joseph Watkins. I'm drumming with the George Lewis jazz band.

ctx.x: Joseph Watkins Okay, it's going. Do you want to give your name?
All right. My name is Joseph Watkins. I'm drumming with the George Lewis jazz band. At the present time, been waiting for about 12 or 13 years.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1969-03-24
items.q: he said, Joe, he said, how about joining up with me? Well, that was after he had come back from New York. That was in 1945. I said, yeah, I said, I'll play with you until somebody better comes along. He said, all right, he said, you can play all jobs with me.

ctx.x: What sort of date was this? Huh? What date was this about?

Oh, that was around in the 1940s. Yeah, in the 1940s, because I was living across the street at the time, at 825 North Galvestre. And the first job that, after he found out that I was playing that good, Herbert Moran, one of our old time trumpet men, he was a wonderful jazz man on the trumpet. He left Chicago and came back home. And he heard me play. He said, Joe, he said, why don't you try to stick with the drums? I said, well, if I'm playing that good, I said, I don't mind sticking with it, but if I'm bad, I…
Yes. Would that be the Parisian Room?

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: You had the drummer, Joe Watkins.

ctx.x: Could you describe the setup at the... this was at the Beverly Capitol? Mm-hmm. The setup there, the atmosphere, clientele, prices, the way the band was received, general atmosphere of the... of the club and so on.

It was strictly at over 21 places. Strictly cocktail, there was a little Chinese restaurant next door. Um... As you looked at the stage, the... they had a grand piano for Purnell. And he... as you looked at the... well... as you looked at the stage, he was on the right. The banjo was just in front of him, slightly to the left. And then going across the front of the stage was George Lewis, uh... Kid Howard, and Jim Robinson. Directly in the center behind the band, it was kind of... it was in a corner. You had the…
Uh... what about the, um... was there any dancing?
